item.text: {"results":[{"pair_id":"J02690","case1_error":"Gives unsupported final answer 6186 after correct formulas, which yield 859.","case2_error":"Gives unsupported final answer 150 after correct formulas, which yield 180.","reason":"Both present correct setups followed by incorrect final numbers without showing the numerical evaluation.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J02691","case1_error":"Treats 70% cheaper as costing 70% of the original price instead of 30%.","case2_error":"Reports net spending of $23 as money remaining, without subtracting it from the initial $74.","reason":"The first misinterprets a percentage reduction; the second answers spending instead of remaining money.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02692","case1_error":"Applies the stated four overtime hours to each of five days, multiplying the overtime payment fivefold.","case2_error":"Uses $1 per bead instead of $1 per ten beads, producing $1800 instead of $180.","reason":"The first repeats a total overtime allowance across days; the second incorrectly converts a bulk price into a per-item rate.","judgment":"different"},{"pair_id":"J02693","case1_error":"Ignores the stated $18 remaining and assigns all $38 after necessities to taxes.","case2_error":"Ignores the required $7 subway fare when determining money available for apples.","reason":"Both allocate the entire intermediate balance to the target expense without subtracting an explicitly required reserved amount.","judgment":"same"},{"pair_id":"J02694","case1_error":"Substitutes one Monday counting occurrence for the two Tuesday tile-counting occurrences, obtaining 4.","case2_error":"Triples an already combined bedroom duration for the living room and divides work among four people instead of three.","reason":"The first selects a count from the wrong day; the second misapplies a combined-duration relation and miscounts workers.","judgment":"different"}]}
